patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` does not apply cleanly because its unrelated `misc_parsers.cpp` hunk diverges, but the authoritative `n132/arvo:22978-fix` image carries the repaired `LibRaw_buffer_datastream::gets()` logic. On the original 127-byte no-newline PoC, the fixed build reaches `terminator_guard` with `dest_offset == last_valid_index` and no `terminator_write` follows (`guarded`). The adjacent `length_126_no_newline` witness executes the same preincrement branch with `126 < 127` on both versions, supplying the fixed-side genuine witness.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: Immediately before the preincrement terminator store `*(++pdest) = 0;`, `LibRaw_buffer_datastream::gets()` must prove that one byte of destination capacity remains beyond the current payload offset, i.e. `(pdest - str) < (sz - 1)`. The vulnerable post-loop guard checks only `< sz`, so it approves the branch even when `pdest` is already at the last in-bounds slot.
root_cause_criterion.description: The selected root obligation is the missing spare-slot guard on the vulnerable preincrement terminator branch. In the crashing original execution the latest `terminator_guard` event records `dest_offset=127` and `last_valid_index=127`, so the required predicate is false while the protected `terminator_write` still executes. In the authoritative fixed image the same original input is `guarded`, and the adjacent `length_126_no_newline` witness executes the protected branch genuinely with `dest_offset=126 < 127`.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The fixed original is guarded because the repaired source keeps the `*(++pdest)=0` branch disabled when the buffer is exactly full and uses the safe fallback instead. The closest source-grounded mutation is the one-byte-shorter no-newline witness `length_126_no_newline`, which re-enters the same branch with one spare slot remaining and therefore verifies the required assertion genuinely.

nodes.state: At the selected sink event, the preincremented terminator index exceeds the last valid destination index. The vulnerable original trace records `terminator_index=128` with `last_valid_index=127`, so `*(++pdest) = 0;` targets the first byte past `parse_rollei()`'s 128-byte stack buffer.

edges.relation: The same `pdest` pointer observed by the vulnerable post-loop guard is the pointer immediately preincremented and written through by `*(++pdest) = 0;`, so the guard's exact full-buffer state is what reaches the sanitizer sink.
